'''''Erysimum capitatum''''' is a species of [[Erysimum|wallflower]] known commonly as the '''sanddune wallflower''', '''western wallflower''', or '''prairie rocket'''.

This species can be found in regions across [[North America]], from the [[Great Lakes]] to the [[West Coast of the United States]].  Some varieties have an extremely narrow distribution, especially those [[endemism|endemic]] to [[California]].

==Description==
''Erysimum capitatum'' is a [[mustard plant|mustard]]-like plant with thin, erect stems growing from a basal [[rosette (botany)|rosette]] and topped with dense bunches of variably colored flowers.  Flowers are most typically bright golden, yellow, or tangerine-colored, but plants in some populations may have red, white or purple flowers.   Each flower has four flat [[petal]]s. [[Seed pod]]s are nearly parallel to the stem. It is a biennial herb and its native habitats include plains, foothills, and high elevation coniferous forests.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center - The University of Texas at Austin|url=https://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=erca14|access-date=2021-11-11|website=www.wildflower.org}}</ref> The Latin specific epithet ''capitatum'' refers to the head-like shape of the flower cluster or the knobby stigma.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Erysimum capitatum - Plant Finder|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?taxonid=278053&isprofile=0&n=1|access-date=2021-11-11|website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}}</ref>

===Subspecies===
There are varieties or [[subspecies]] of this plant. Some are listed [[endangered species]]. For example, ''Erysimum capitatum'' var. ''angustatum'', the Contra Costa wallflower, is an endangered plant in the state of [[California]].  The varieties include:

*''E. c.'' var. ''angustatum''—Contra Costa wallflower; endemic to California, endangered species.<ref>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-taxon=Erysimum+capitatum+var.+angustatum&one=T Calflora: ''Erysimum capitatum'' var. ''angustatum'']</ref><ref>[http://www.rareplants.cnps.org/detail/790.html CNPS Inventory: Endangered Plant details: ''Erysimum capitatum'' var. ''angustatum'']</ref>
*''E. c.'' var. ''bealianum''—Sanddune wallflower; [[Mojave Desert]], California.<ref>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=3473 Calflora: ''Erysimum capitatum'' var. ''bealianum'']</ref>
*''E. c.'' var. ''capitatum''—Western wallflower; flowers from May to July, widely distributed across Colorado and Utah.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20070717201245/http://herbarium.uvsc.edu/Virtual/search.asp?taxon=Erysimum+capitatum|title=Utah Valley State College Herbarium}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://herbarium.uvu.edu/Virtual/search.asp?taxon=Erysimum+capitatum|title=UVU Virtual Herbarium|work=Utah Valley University Herbarium|publisher=Utah Valley University|accessdate=2 May 2014|archive-date=2 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502120547/http://herbarium.uvu.edu/Virtual/search.asp?taxon=Erysimum+capitatum|url-status=dead}}</ref> 
*''E. c.'' var. ''lompocense''—San Luis Obispo wallflower; endemic to California.<ref>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=9944 Calflora: ''Erysimum capitatum'' var. ''lompocense'']</ref>
*''E. c.'' var. ''perenne'' (syn: ''Erysimum perenne'')—Sanddune wallflower; endemic to California.<ref>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=11678 Calflora: ''Erysimum perenne'']</ref>
*''E. c.'' var. ''purshii''—Pursh's wallflower; [[Western United States]].<ref>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=9946 Calflora: ''Erysimum capitatum'' var. ''purshii'']</ref>

==Pollinators==
Little information on this wallflower species relationship with pollinators exists. Andrew Moldenke studied a population  of ''Erysimum capitatum'' var. ''perenne'' in Subalpine Talus Fell Scree of the Timberland Hall Area ({{convert|2900|-|3500|m|ft}} elevation). He observed 13 species of flower visitors, although over 80% of the visits to the flowers were performed by two ant species, ''Formica lasioides'' and one from the ''[[Formica fusca]]'' group.

==Cultivation==
''Erysimum capitatum'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.laspilitas.com/nature-of-california/plants/erysimum-capitatum |work = Las Pilitas Nursery | title = ''Erysimum capitatum'', Western Wallflower | accessdate = 2013-02-14}}</ref> It is an attractive [[perennial]], can be variable in appearance, and is used in [[butterfly gardening]].

==Uses==
In [[Zuni ethnobotany]], an infusion of the whole plant is used externally for muscle aches. The flower and the fruit are eaten as an emetic for stomach aches.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Camazine|first=Scott|author2=Robert A. Bye|title=A Study Of The Medical Ethnobotany Of The Zuni Indians of New Mexico|journal=Journal of Ethnopharmacology|date=1980|volume=2|issue=4|pages=365–88|pmid=6893476|doi=10.1016/S0378-8741(80)81017-8}}</ref>
